content: The provided text is a detailed list of drug interactions involving cimetidine, a histamine H2-receptor antagonist, and various other medications. 1. Cimetidine and Fosphenytoin: Cimetidine increases the plasma levels and effects of fosphenytoin by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 2. Cimetidine and Fostamatinib: Fostamatinib increases the levels and effects of cimetidine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for potential toxicities, especially with P-gp substrates, and consider dose adjustments if necessary. 3. Cimetidine and Fostemsavir: Fostemsavir increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Avoid coadministration if possible, or adjust the dose of BCRP substrates. Monitor therapy closely. 4. Cimetidine and Gefitinib: Cimetidine reduces gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration of gefitinib and H2-antagonists by at least 6 hours. Use caution and monitor. 5. Cimetidine and Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases cimetidine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor therapy. 6. Cimetidine and Glipizide: Cimetidine increases glipizide levels by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 7. Cimetidine and Glyburide: Cimetidine increases glyburide levels by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Cimetidine and Haloperidol: Cimetidine increases haloperidol levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Cimetidine and Hydrocodone: Cimetidine increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Hydromorphone, a minor metabolite of hydrocodone, may contribute to the overall analgesic effect. Use caution and monitor therapy. 10. Cimetidine and Hydromorphone: Cimetidine increases hydromorphone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 11. Cimetidine and Iloperidone: Cimetidine increases iloperidone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 12. Cimetidine and Imatinib: Cimetidine increases imatinib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 13. Cimetidine and Imipramine: Cimetidine increases imipramine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 14. Cimetidine and Iron Dextran Complex: Cimetidine reduces iron dextran complex levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 15. Cimetidine and Iron Sucrose: Cimetidine reduces iron sucrose levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Cimetidine and Isavuconazonium Sulfate: Cimetidine increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Cimetidine and Isoniazid: Isoniazid increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Cimetidine and Isradipine: Cimetidine increases isradipine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Cimetidine and Istradefylline: Istradefylline increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Clinical trials have shown increased peak levels and AUC of P-gp substrates. Consider dose reduction of sensitive P-gp substrates. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Cimetidine and Itraconazole: Cimetidine reduces itraconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Administer acid-neutralizing agents at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. When coadministered with cimetidine, use non-diet cola to increase gastric acidity. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Cimetidine and Ivacaftor: Cimetidine increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the ivacaftor dose when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to specific ivacaftor-containing product guidelines for dosage adjustments. Use caution and monitor therapy. 22. Cimetidine and Ketoconazole: Cimetidine increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 23. Cimetidine and Lapatinib: Cimetidine reduces lapatinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Cimetidine and Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Cimetidine reduces ledipasvir levels due to decreased solubility at higher pH levels. Administer H2-receptor antagonists simultaneously or 12 hours apart from ledipasvir/sofosbuvir at doses comparable to famotidine 40 mg BID. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Cimetidine and Lemborexant: Cimetidine increases lemborexant levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Cimetidine and Levoketoconazole: Cimetidine increases levoketoconazole levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Cimetidine and Lidocaine: Cimetidine increases lidocaine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Cimetidine and Lomitapide: Lomitapide increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Consider reducing the dose of cimetidine when used concomitantly with lomitapide. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 29. Cimetidine and Lomustine: Cimetidine decreases lomustine metabolism, potentially enhancing myelotoxicity. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Cimetidine and Lonafarnib: Lonafarnib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Monitor for adverse reactions when coadministered with P-gp substrates, as minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. Reduce P-gp substrate doses if needed. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Cimetidine and Lurasidone: Cimetidine increases lurasidone levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. The manufacturer recommends reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Monitor for lurasidone-related adverse reactions. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 32. Cimetidine and Mavacamten: Cimetidine increases mavacamten levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C19 metabolism. Initiation of weak CYP2C19 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 33. Cimetidine and Mavorixafor: Mavorixafor increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution if mavorixafor is coadministered with sensitive P-gp substrates, as minimal substrate concentration changes may lead to serious adverse effects. Use caution and monitor therapy. 34. Cimetidine and Mebendazole: Cimetidine increases mebendazole levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 35. Cimetidine and Mefloquine: Cimetidine increases mefloquine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Cimetidine and Melatonin: Cimetidine increases melatonin levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor melatonin effects when coadministered with moderate CYP1A2 inhibitors. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Cimetidine and Memantine: Cimetidine increases memantine levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Cimetidine and Metformin: Cimetidine increases metformin levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 39. Cimetidine and Methamphetamine: Cimetidine increases methamphetamine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 40. Cimetidine and Methylphenidate: Cimetidine decreases methylphenidate effects by enhancing gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy and monitor closely. For extended-release methylphenidate capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), consider separating administration of antacids or acid suppressants to avoid altering drug release. 41. Cimetidine and Metoprolol: Cimetidine increases metoprolol levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 42. Cimetidine and Mexiletine: Cimetidine increases mexiletine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 43. Cimetidine and Midazolam (Intranasal): Cimetidine increases midazolam levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with mild CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation. Use caution and monitor therapy. 44. Cimetidine and Midodrine: Cimetidine increases midodrine levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 45. Cimetidine and Mizolastine: Cimetidine increases mizolastine levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 46. Cimetidine and Momelotinib: Momelotinib increases cimetidine toxicity due to plasma protein binding competition. Momelotinib, a BCRP inhibitor, may increase exposure to BCRP substrates, raising the risk of adverse reactions. Dose adjustment of other BCRP substrates may be necessary. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Cimetidine and Morphine: Cimetidine increases morphine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 48. Cimetidine and Nateglinide: Cimetidine increases nateglinide levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 49. Cimetidine and Nebivolol: Cimetidine increases nebivolol levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 50. Cimetidine and Nelfinavir: Cimetidine increases nelfinavir levels by raising gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 51. Cimetidine and Nicotine (Inhaled): Cimetidine increases nicotine levels by decreasing renal clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 52. Cimetidine and Nicotine (Intranasal): Cimetidine increases nicotine levels by decreasing metabolism and renal clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 53. Cimetidine and Nifedipine: Cimetidine increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 54. Cimetidine and Nilotinib: Cimetidine reduces nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Avoid this interaction by administering H2 antagonists 10 hours after or 2 hours before nilotinib. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 55. Cimetidine and Nimodipine: Cimetidine increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 56. Cimetidine and Nortriptyline: Cimetidine increases nortriptyline levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 57. Cimetidine and Olanzapine: Cimetidine increases olanzapine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 58. Cimetidine and Oliceridine: Cimetidine increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. If coadministration is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 59. Cimetidine and Otesaconazole: Otesaconazole increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting BCRP transporters. Use the lowest starting dose of BCRP substrates or consider reducing the BCRP substrate dose. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 60. Cimetidine and Oxybutynin: Cimetidine increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 61. Cimetidine and Oxycodone: Cimetidine increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 62. Cimetidine and Oxymorphone: Cimetidine increases oxymorphone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 63. Cimetidine and Paclitaxel: Cimetidine increases paclitaxel levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 64. Cimetidine and Paclitaxel (Protein-Bound): Cimetidine increases protein-bound paclitaxel levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 65. Cimetidine and Palbociclib: Cimetidine increases palbociclib levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 66. Cimetidine and Parecoxib: Cimetidine increases parecoxib levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 67. Cimetidine and Paroxetine: Cimetidine increases paroxetine levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 68. Cimetidine and Pentoxifylline: Cimetidine increases pentoxifylline levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 69. Cimetidine and Phenytoin: Cimetidine increases phenytoin levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 70. Cimetidine and Pimozide: Cimetidine increases pimozide levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 71. Cimetidine and Pioglitazone: Cimetidine increases pioglitazone levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 72. Cimetidine and Polysaccharide Iron: Cimetidine reduces polysaccharide iron levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 73. Cimetidine and Ponatinib: Ponatinib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor therapy. 74. Cimetidine and Posaconazole: Cimetidine reduces posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Use caution and monitor therapy. 75. Cimetidine and Pramipexole: Cimetidine increases pramipexole levels due to competition for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor therapy. 76. Cimetidine and Praziquantel: Cimetidine increases praziquantel levels by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 77. Cimetidine and Propafenone: Cimetidine increases propafenone levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 78. Cimetidine and Propranolol: Cimetidine increases propranolol levels by inhibiting hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 79. Cimetidine and Quinine: Cimetidine increases quinine levels by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy.
